Unlike c-Si module production, which combines individual cells in strings, CdTe modules are composed of one solid unit of cells (i.e., monolithically integrated) directly deposited on the front glass. This section only discusses U.S. company First Solar, because it is the only large-scale producer of CdTe PV. Direct inputs to CdTe module production are discussed, except for CdTe powder and glass, which are the focus of subsequent sections. Figure 37 shows a simplified supply chain diagram based on NLR research (Smith, Woodhouse, Horowitz, et al. 2021a; Scarpulla et al. 2023) as well as more recent documentation of module composition (First Solar 2024e). 35 Given the volume of CdTe modules produced and sold by First Solar over the past several years and the weighting in revenue toward the United States, EIA may be underrepresenting U.S. CdTe installed capacity. For example, EIA reported 7.8 GW of CdTe installed in 2024, while global First Solar production has exceeded that level since 2021, dc reaching 12 GW in 2023 and 15 GW in 2024. The three most likely explanations are: (1) CdTe modules are dc dc combined with c-Si panels in systems only reported as using c-Si panels. While 600 MW of plants reported dc combined use in 2024, discussions with some developers indicate this number may be higher. (2) U.S. developers are stockpiling First Solar modules for use in future systems. Given the previous uncertainty in tax credits, developers may have purchased 5% of the cost of future PV systems to safe harbor projects over the next 4 years. (3) First Solar has reported warranty claims, so some production could be module replacements (or repowering of existing facilities). 52 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Simplified supply chain diagram for CdTe module production 3.3.1 Technology Trends for CdTe Modules Because First Solar is the only large-scale producer of CdTe PV, this section focuses on First Solar’s technology trends. In 2024, 62% of First Solar’s global production was for the Series 6 model, while 38% was for Series 7 (Figure 38). The Series 7 model is larger and more efficient but does not have a bifacial option, unlike the Series 6 (Table 7). Industry interviews indicate that the Series 7 platform is intended for monofacial and bifacial products, but monofacial products were launched first given the rapid capacity expansion.36 Another primary distinction between the two products is the frame and mounting format (Table 7). Series 7 modules are technically frameless but include steel rails for mounting, while the Series 6 has an aluminum frame that incorporates a mounting mechanism.
